error_text: error[E0308]: mismatched types --> src/frame.rs:88 | expected `i32`, found `String`
gold_fix: The sensor firmware sends `fps` as a JSON string, not a number; parse it with fps.parse::<i32>()? before use — do NOT just cast, the value arrives quoted.
memory: E0308 in camera-driver: the sensor firmware sends `fps` as a JSON string. Fix: fps.parse::<i32>()? before assigning; a plain `as i32` cast won't compile because the source is a String.

error_text: thread 'main' panicked at 'index out of bounds: the len is 100 but the index is 100', src/ring.rs:71
gold_fix: The ring buffer masks the index with `& (cap - 1)`, so capacity MUST be a power of two; someone set it to 100. Set capacity to 128.
memory: ring.rs panic 'index out of bounds': the ring buffer masks with & (cap-1), so cap must be a power of two. Was set to 100 → set it to 128.

error_text: test test_frame_pipeline::concurrent_decode ... FAILED (then passed on retry)
gold_fix: A shared `static CAMERA_HANDLE` is reused across tests; the fix was to make it thread_local, not to add a retry. Retrying only hides it.
memory: Flaky test_frame_pipeline: a shared `static CAMERA_HANDLE` was mutated by concurrent tests. Fix: made CAMERA_HANDLE thread_local. (Adding a retry hid it, didn't fix it.)

gold_fix: OOM on the 8GB Jetson during the Tauri/WebKit build: set CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 and use the mold linker; the default parallelism exhausts RAM only on that build.

gold_fix: The systemd unit on the Jetson sets MEMORYWHALE_TOKEN, so mw-serve requires ?token=…; the token is in /etc/memorywhale/token. Append ?token=<that>.
memory: mw-serve 401 on the Jetson: the systemd unit exports MEMORYWHALE_TOKEN, so a token is required. Fix: visit with ?token=<value from /etc/memorywhale/token>.

error_text: servo overshoots target angle by ~4% consistently
gold_fix: The PCA9685 on our board revision runs ~4% fast; write the CALIB register (0x1A) with the measured offset — it's a hardware clock drift, not a code bug.
memory: Servo overshoot ~4%: the PCA9685 clock on rev-B boards runs fast. Fix: calibrate via CALIB register 0x1A; it's hardware drift, no code change fixes it.

gold_fix: A stale `mw --live` process still holds the SQLite lock; kill it (ps aux | grep mw-run). The durable fix already added busy_timeout, but an orphaned recorder still blocks.
memory: 'database is locked' on mw --live: a stale mw-run recorder holds the lock. Fix: kill the orphaned process (ps aux | grep mw). busy_timeout helps but an orphan still blocks.

gold_fix: You tagged before the release workflow's bump-formula job updated the sha; the formula points at the old tarball. Re-run the release workflow or pull the formula bump from main.
memory: brew SHA256 mismatch after release: the formula's sha is bumped by CI AFTER the tag, so a fresh tag briefly has a stale sha. Fix: wait for / re-run the bump-formula job, or git pull main.

memory: cargo publish 'no matching mw-memory version': publish mw-memory before memorywhale-cli — the versioned path dep must resolve from crates.io. Also the CI publish step needs pipefail or a failed publish silently passes.

gold_fix: An earlier migration pinned user_version to the LATEST constant instead of its own literal, so it jumped the DB past migration 4 and skipped it. Fix the pin to the literal version and re-run.
memory: 'no such column: error_fingerprint': a migration pinned PRAGMA user_version to LATEST_SCHEMA_VERSION instead of its own literal, skipping migration 4 on some DBs. Fix: pin each migration to its literal version.

error_text: mw: mempalace unavailable (`mempalace-mcp` does not expose a `search` tool); using the local engine
gold_fix: The real MemPalace server's search tool is named `mempalace_search`, not `search`; set `mempalace_tool = "mempalace_search"` in config.toml.
memory: mempalace 'does not expose a search tool': the real server's tool is mempalace_search, not search. Fix: mempalace_tool = "mempalace_search" in config.toml.

error_text: error: couldn't read src/bin/../../../../linux/shell/memorywhale.sh: No such file or directory
gold_fix: include_str! reached outside the crate; cargo publish only packages crate files. Move the shell assets inside crates/mw-cli/ and point include_str! at the in-crate copy.
memory: cargo publish 'couldn't read ../../../../linux/shell/...': include_str! reached outside the crate, which the package tarball excludes. Fix: moved the shell hooks into crates/mw-cli/shell/ and pointed include_str! there.
